headline: Cell-type separability, not algorithm choice, predicts scRNA annotation accuracy
label: Single Cell Computational Benchmarking
summary: Benchmarking and quality-control studies across scRNA-seq, spatial, and splicing modalities are now quantifying which analysis choices drive accuracy.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational validation of single-cell and related profiling data. A factorial benchmark of 63 scRNA-seq annotation tools across seven families finds that cell-type separability in embedding space predicts accuracy more than algorithm choice, while scDiagnostics targets ambiguous or conflicting reference-to-query labels directly. Quality control is addressed at the read and cell level: Pattern-Filter validates read structure before alignment, removing 2-18% of reads, and SingleCellMQC provides modality-aware QC across scRNA-seq, ADT and TCR/BCR data. Spatial benchmarking extends this scrutiny, with nine CNA inference methods evaluated on 69 spatial transcriptomics sections from six cancers, where no single method performed best across conditions. On the isoform side, scASprofiler imputes sparse splice-junction counts, and Spl-ISO-Seq2 enables 500-nm spatial long-read isoform sequencing. What is distinctive is the shift toward systematic, multi-method evaluation of analysis choices rather than single-method claims.
